cohort: The study included 3,652 postpartum participants (681 infected, 2,971 uninfected) from two tertiary hospitals in China, classified based on prenatal SARS-CoV-2 antigen results.
finding: Prenatal SARS-CoV-2 infection was not associated with an increased risk of postpartum LUTS but independently altered pelvic floor muscle electromyographic activity.
mod_finding: The independent alteration of pelvic floor muscle electromyographic activity due to SARS-CoV-2 infection was observed regardless of the delivery mode.
